forks.decision: External tasks run fully native with a local checkout without upstream history, a local uv venv or Go/Rust toolchain, and our replay of the instance's FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS tests; no Docker
One evolutionary loop mutates code and text; a candidate is a commit
The loop engine is GEPA optimize_anything with repeat runs on frontier candidates
The loop may mutate only src and prompts; winners land as human-reviewed draft PRs
The judge labels per-task applicability and critiques each rollout for reflection only; grader correctness is the only objective
The Phase 4 power gate is retired; every paid run requires an explicit spend ceiling

contradictions: Cross-curd invariant 2 (spec line 96) says reflective records 'never' carry 'ground-truth strings'. AC-2 (line 115) and test_reflective_record_has_untruncated_tool_io (line 128) require every tool call's full input and output in those same records. For the three local hard tasks, both cannot hold. Their ground truth is code identifiers that every correct rollout must emit: rg_trait_implementors requires 'Matcher', 'find_at', 'RegexMatcher' (benchmark/tasks/ripgrep_tasks.py:26), and 'Matcher' and 'find_at' already appear in its prompt (ripgrep_tasks.py:17-19). rg_search_dispatch requires 'ReadByLine', 'MultiLine', 'Sink', 'glue.rs' (ripgrep_tasks.py:80). Grading substring-matches these strings in the final answer (benchmark/tasks/base.py:174-180). The answer is stored in result_text (benchmark/run.py:852) and the sidecar, and the same identifiers fill any search or read output over ripgrep. The AC-2 test fails when any record 'contains SECRET_GT' seeded 'in the task ground truth' (line 128), but the parent never says whether the canned sidecar's agent output may contain it. So a Cook either substring-redacts ground truth out of prompts, tool outputs, and answers, which mangles the raw records G-4 depends on and breaks AC-2's full-I/O clause, or keeps them, which breaks the invariant as written. Scope the invariant to grader-side fields and artifacts (correctness_reason, the GroundTruth/required_strings field, gold patch, held-out test files and their output), and make the AC-2 fixture state that agent-produced occurrences are kept.
acceptance_gaps: No parent test observes the positive branch of G-5 ('run once, stored, and reused'). The AC-3 row (spec line 129) has two tests. test_second_evolve_buys_no_baseline fails only when the second run records a baseline-arm call. test_env_drift_refuses_without_refreeze fails only when a drifted second run starts. Neither asserts that the first run buys each baseline cell exactly once and stores it, or that an unchanged second run actually starts and completes. A broken evolve.main whose run key or env fingerprint is not deterministic across invocations (for example one that hashes a temp worktree path or timestamp) refuses every second run as drift. That run makes no baseline-arm call, so it passes both tests, while baselines are never reused and must be re-bought through --refreeze-baselines on every run. The AC-8 test (line 134) uses a pre-seeded store and cannot catch this. Add a positive control: on an empty store, the first evolve.main records exactly one stubbed baseline-arm call per baseline cell, and the unchanged second run starts, finishes, and reuses those rows with reused: true.
